verdict: Mostly confirmed, with 12 corrections (11 to numbers, wording or scope; 1 to the P-A proof) and 1 important omission. The instrumented copy is the frozen learner (byte-identical rebuild; its AST equals dfg13.py's once the 65 hook statements are removed). Every headline count of A1, A2 and B reproduces from the raw records with my own code. 17 independent refits of the frozen module (8 A1, 7 A2, 2 B; own data generation) equal the records or result files bit for bit. P-A and P-A' hold, though P-A's proof mishandles the s clipping. The round-0 FLOP formula is exact on all 825 recorded _fit calls. Corrections: (1) 'every fit was checked' (572 A1 and 800 cascade fits were not); (2) the 'sum-block tests never passed' holds only for the final fits; two default fold fits on noise admitted sum blocks in round 0; (3) 238 forced fold fits hold a test-passed feature but only 229 after a forced one (also 12->10, 14->12, 150->143); (4) the linear block's null rate is close to, not 'exactly', the chi^2_d tail (0.845% vs 0.921% at d = 30); (5) the spectral rates quoted come from the small samples: about 5.3% and 47%, not 5.7% and 48%; (6) P(>= 2 degree-1 passes in 440) = 0.053, not 0.082, and all 6 classes are compatible with the Gaussian approximation; (7) removing the spurious terms changes the mean error by up to 0.0002, not 0.0001, from n = 128 on; (8) the largest fit (0.519) spends 37% on the readout, not 41-47%; (9) the 0.75 GFLOP/s sum-block rate is the final fits' rate (0.27 inside the fold fits); (10) m6 = 73, not min(n, 147), at n = 128-512; (11) one of the 221 cascade local admissions did not come after two forced characters. Omission: the spectral block's biased-label null pass rate grows steeply with d and with label bias (d = 120, p = 0.8: 99% at n = 512 and 67% at n = 1024; d = 30, p = 0.9: 39% at n = 128), which the report's 'falling to 0 by n = 1024/4096' leaves out.

claims.claim: S0: dfg13_instr.py is dfg13.py (md5 69cabe5c...) with 64 lines added and none changed; rebuilding it with make_instr.py gives the same file byte for byte (md5 be56ce50...); the hooks only read.
claims.evidence: I rebuilt it with a scratch copy of make_instr.py, redirecting only the output path: md5 be56ce50963f2f7fc513ab82616cbcc7, byte-identical by cmp. diff dfg13.py dfg13_instr.py shows 64 added lines, 0 removed or changed, all of them _P.<hook>(...) or the recorder import. AST check: deleting the 65 _P.* expression statements (on 64 lines; one line holds two) and the import gives an AST identical to dfg13.py's, so no insertion changes block structure. The hook arguments call only len(). calib_rec.Rec only reads fl[0], the process clock and its arguments, and writes only to its own dicts and lists.

Seven of them are cells the report never checked: 30:0.8:64:7, 30:0.8:16384:18, 30:0.5:256:13, 60:0.5:512:5, 60:0.8:256:5, 30:0.5:4096:11 and 60:0.5:8192:4.

That the copy is the frozen learner for every fit follows from the AST equivalence and the read-only hooks, not from the checks.

claims.claim: P-A (Proved): on labels independent of iid uniform inputs, in round 0 of any _fit call each global character class of degree k (1-4; 5-6 in the subsample search) passes with probability <= delta/(2K) = 0.0125; the six classes together <= 0.075.
claims.evidence: The statement holds; I checked it line by line against dfg13.py. lsfit's ridge is zero on the constant, so r = y - sum(y)/(n + 1e-9). thr() uses self.K = 4 in every round. The degree-3 loop over a < d-2 and the degree-4 loop over pairs with b < d-2 together cover all C(d,3) and C(d,4) subsets. The degree-5/6 G entries over disjoint (T1, T2) equal mean(r chi_{T1 u T2}). thr_m reduces to c rms(r_1..m) sqrt(2L/m). Hoeffding plus the union bound give 2N exp(-L) = delta/(2K). The bound also covers fold fits (fold rows chosen by an rng independent of X and y) and both CV variants (round 0 is identical in both). Proof gap: s = sqrt(max(mean r^2, 1e-12)) is never below 1e-6, because sqrt(1e-12) evaluates to exactly 1e-06, so the step '(if s < 1e-6 the loop stops before any test)' is vacuous. When all labels are equal, the m = n tests run with s = 1e-6 > rms(r), and the claimed 'iff |sum r chi| > c sqrt(2L sum r^2)' fails. Two A1 final fits are such cases (30:0.8:16:14 and :19, recorded round-0 s = 1e-06; nothing passed).
claims.correction: The statement stands. The proof should say: the m = n tests use s = max(rms(r), 1e-6) >= rms(r), so their pass event is contained in the event with s = rms(r), and the m < n tests use rms(r_1..m) exactly. The bound then follows in all cases, including all-equal labels.

claims.claim: P-A' (Proved): if y depends only on inputs R, in round 0 P(some chi_S with S not inside R passes) <= (N_irr/N) delta/(2K) per class.
claims.evidence: Checked each step: r is a function of the R-columns; for j in S outside R, conditioning on y and on every other column leaves column j iid uniform, so the sum is a weighted Rademacher sum with weights of total square sum(r^2); the thresholds depend on r only. Like P-A, it needs iid uniform rows, which the A2 data satisfy (harness.train_data), and holds in learner coordinates under Permuted.

claims.claim: S1.3: '5 of 6 classes are compatible with the ~0.001 of the Gaussian approximation (degree 1: 2/440 where 0.5 is expected)'; the MC gives 0.108% per degree-1 test, so 2 or more passes in 440 tests has probability 0.082.
claims.evidence: I computed the degree-1 class's null pass probability exactly for every (p, n): a binomial convolution conditional on the labels, validated against simulation at lower thresholds within 1 SE. It is 0 at n = 16, 0.00004-0.00045 at n = 32, 0.0002-0.0008 at n = 64 and about 0.00113 for large n. The average over the report's four MC cells is 0.094%, consistent with its 0.108%.
claims.correction: With the per-(p, n) rates, the expected number of degree-1 passes in the 440 tests is 0.37 and P(X >= 2) = 0.053, not 0.082; the pooled rate overstates the small-n cells. Degree 1 is also compatible: its 95% CI (0.0006-0.016) contains 0.0012, so all 6 classes are compatible.

claims.claim: Linear block: null pass rate 0.84% (d = 30) and 1.04% (d = 60) in 80000-draw nulls; observed 2/360 and 4/160; short answer: it 'passes at the exact chi^2_d tail of its Laurent-Massart threshold'.
claims.evidence: The MC numbers and binomial p-values (0.81, 0.087) recompute. My own null MC, which mirrors _fit (constant fit with the 1e-9 term, inputs already passing excluded, room rule n >= 2(1+k)), gives 239/28000 = 0.85% at d = 30 and 0.95% at d = 60. The exact tails are 0.921% and 1.051%.
claims.correction: At d = 30 the rate is not exactly the chi^2_30 tail. Pooling 108000 draws gives 0.845% (95% CI 0.79-0.90%), which excludes 0.921%. The statistic is a sum of squared Rademacher sums, whose tail is lighter than chi^2_d. Say 'close to the chi^2_d tail (0.84% against 0.92% at d = 30; 1.04% against 1.05% at d = 60), about 1/10 of delta'.

Against the delta = 0.1 in its own margin factor it fails only at d = 60, and the 'falling to 0' holds only for the two (d, p) settings measured (see omissions).

omissions: The spectral block's false-admission rate on biased residuals grows steeply with d and with label bias, and the report measures only d in {30, 60} and p in {0.5, 0.8}. My null MC (mirroring _fit's round 0) gives, at d = 120 with P(y=1) = 0.8, 397/400 passes (99%) at n = 512 (the first grid n >= 4d) and 202/300 (67%) at n = 1024; at d = 30 with P(y=1) = 0.9, 39% at n = 128 and 11% at n = 256 (0/300 at d = 120, p = 0.5). The report's own Marchenko-Pastur heuristic predicts this: at n = 4d the minority edge is fixed, while DFG's margin factor 1 + sqrt(2 ln 10/d) shrinks with d. 'Falling to 0 by n = 1024 (d = 30) and 4096 (d = 60)' does not carry over to the designed_d120 suite or to strongly biased targets (e.g. and3, P(y=1) = 1/8). The 15 spurious spectral features at n = 128-256 in A2 are plausibly this effect; the report does not connect them.
The sum-block test is not shown to be calibrated on noise. It passed in round 0 in 2 default fold fits (d = 30, p = 0.8), and the report's 'never passed' summary omits the fold fits.

The empirical identity check covers 88 of the 660 A1 fits and none of the 800 cascade fits. The equivalence argument (AST plus read-only hooks) should be stated as the reason the uncovered fits are trustworthy.

P-A's proof does not handle the s floor (s = max(rms r, 1e-6); the 's < 1e-6' break can never fire). The all-labels-equal case actually occurs: in 2 A1 final fits, and in 24 fold training sets (48 fold fits, both variants) at p = 0.8 with n = 16 and 32.

The fold-fit records keep neither the round of each admission nor the characters' sets. So 'after the forced ones' and 'chi_A chi_B' can be checked for the evaluation's own fold fits only indirectly (by pairing with the default fold fits, and by degree sums: 185 of 205 provable). Keeping per-round 'added' in the fold records would settle it.
The linear block's statistic, a sum of squared Rademacher sums, has a lighter tail than chi^2_d. That is why its d = 30 null rate is about 8% below the chi^2_30 tail; the report does not say why.

Provenance: the first 32 B records (written before the restart) lack the 'rep' field that the current calib.py writes, so an earlier calib.py wrote them. Their FLOPs equal the repeats' and my formula, so nothing depends on it, but the report does not mention it.

S1.3's Gaussian reference for degrees 5-6 uses N = C(30,k) independent statistics, although at m = 73-147 rows these N >> m statistics are strongly dependent. It is labelled heuristic, but the comparison of median max-ratios against it says little for those classes.
